subject: Storage zones that improve kitchen flow
hook: Before a single door colour is chosen, the zones go down on paper. Here is how that mapping works.
ig:
Before a single door colour is chosen, the zones go down on paper. Here is how that mapping works.

This is the planning sequence we follow for a kitchen layout, and you can try the first few steps yourself this weekend:

1. List what you own. Be honest about the air fryer.
2. Mark the anchors: sink, hob and fridge.
3. Draw the five zones around them in the order you work.
4. Choose the storage type for each zone: drawers for heavy things, tall units for food, a pull-out bin by the sink.
5. Look for clashes: doors that collide, drawers that block the dishwasher, dead corners.
6. Cook a meal on the drawing. If you cross the room twice, something is in the wrong place.

With the clocks going back tomorrow night, the kitchen is about to get busier in the evenings, so it is a good time to notice what slows you down.

Save this, try steps one and two, and bring your notes to a free consultation. Link in bio.

Planning a new kitchen? Here is a job you can do before anyone comes round, and it costs nothing.

Grab a sheet of paper, sketch where the sink, hob and fridge sit, then list everything that lives in your kitchen. Next, group it: food, crockery, cleaning, prep and cooking. You will quickly see where things are stored miles from where they are used.

That is exactly where we start when designing a bespoke kitchen, before any talk of colours or handles. Swipe through for the full sequence, and see finished work from our workshop here:

Note what can move and what is tied to plumbing, gas or extraction. | F3: Draw the zones — Mark food, crockery, cleaning, prep and cooking around those anchors, in the order you work, so tasks flow one way. | F4: Match storage to each zone — Drawers where you lift things out, such as pans and plates. A tall unit for food. A pull-out bin by the sink. | F5: Find the clashes — Doors that hit each other, drawers that block the dishwasher, corners that go dead. Fix them now, on paper. | F6: Cook a meal on the drawing — Walk through making tea from fridge to plate.
